new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress appears to occur on high tone, and vowel length does not appear to be significant. Tone is contrastive, but may not be as important functionally as it is in the major dialect. Examples of high-low contrast: anami 'leaf' / anami 'nest'; yemi 'he comes' / yemi 'they, them'.

Tone is contrastive, but may not be as important functionally as it is in the major dialect. Examples of high-low contr…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ontena Gadsup is tonal (contrastive high vs low tone, though with a lighter functional load than in the main Akuna dialect); stress is not independent but is perceived on high-toned syllables, i.e. prominence follows lexical tone rather than a fixed position. This agrees with the fuller statement for main-dialect Gadsup in Frantz & Frantz 1966:9 (sec. 2.4): 'Stress is nonphonemic', with syllables bearing high/rising/falling tone, low vowels a e o, or stop onsets sounding more stressed.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement is hedged ('appears to'). The OPD adds that vowel length is not significant in Ontena (unlike the main dialect, where a e o are long).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level OPD observations from an elicited wordlist; no phrase-level discussion. 'Transcription of a recorded passage' section is empty in the printed OPD.
new_statements.identity_note: onte1239 'Ontenu' is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry (ISO 639-3 ont, judged spurious): Ontena is a Gadsup-speaking offshoot community in the Tairora Census Division SW of the main Gadsup area (Frantz 1976:75), and Glottolog folds it into Gadsup [gaj] gads1258. The quoted source is explicitly the ONTENA DIALECT of Gadsup (OPD header 'Gadsup (Ontena dialect) Language [GAJ]', major village Ontena); one line of the OPD writes 'Osena', evidently a typo for Ontena. The fuller stress statement in Frantz & Frantz 1966 (PL A-7:9) is for the main Akuna dialect (Ommomunta/Amomonta village), not Ontena, and is given here only as corroboration. If the catalog keys by Glottolog languoid, this record may belong under gads1258 as a dialect-level entry.

sources.citation: Frantz, Chester I. & Marjorie E. Frantz. 1966. Gadsup phoneme and toneme units. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 5 (Pacific Linguistics A-7), 1-11. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A7.1
sources.note: Main (Akuna) dialect, data from Ommomunta village. p.9 sec. 2.4: 'Stress is nonphonemic. In analogous environments syllables: (1) with a, e, or o have more stress than those with ʌ, i, or u; (2) with high, rising, or falling tones have more stress than those with low; (3) with a phonetic stop onset have more stress than those with nonstop onset. Combinations of these features lead to varying degrees of non-contrastive stress.' Four contrastive tones (high, low, up-glide, down-glide).
